notes: Marker: 형 (hyeong) = older brother of a MALE speaker; a female speaker says 오빠. (Sibling reading with counter 명; the separate in-law honorific use is 형님.)
Marker: 누나 (nuna) = older sister (or close older female) of a MALE speaker; a female speaker says 언니.
Marker: address term 형, used by male speakers to an older brother or close older male; in Korean the kinship address term reveals the SPEAKER's gender.
Marker: 우리 형 — only male speakers call their older brother 형.
Marker: 오빠 (oppa) = older brother (or close older male) of a FEMALE speaker; a male speaker says 형.
Marker: 언니 (eonni) = older sister of a FEMALE speaker; a male speaker says 누나.
Marker: 언니 — used by female speakers for their older sister (or close older female).

glossEn: My older brother is a university student.
notes: Marker: 우리 오빠 — a female speaker's older brother.
저 (jeo, humble 'I') is gender-neutral; Korean first-person pronouns carry no gender.
No kinship term or any other speaker-gender marker.
동생 (dongsaeng, younger sibling) is used by speakers of ANY gender and does not even gender the referent — contrast with 형/누나/오빠/언니.
친구 (friend) is gender-neutral; no speaker-gender marker.

glossEn: Sumi said, 'I miss my older brother.'
notes: 오빠 sits inside the quotation and marks the quoted speaker (수미) as female — not the narrator; the matrix sentence is unmarked.

glossEn: Sumi's older brother is a doctor.
notes: 오빠 is anchored to 수미 (a third party), so it reveals Sumi's gender, not the narrator's.
